title: The US tech industry would be a shadow of itself without immigrants.  First 10 examples that come to mind:  1. Elon Musk...
teaser: According to data, nearly half (44%) of the founders of unicorns are non-US-born, highlighting the massive contribution of immigrants to the U.S. tech industry.
summary: Alec Stapp argues that the U.S. tech industry is heavily reliant on immigrants, pointing to global figures like Elon Musk, Satya Nadella, and Fei-Fei Li. The accompanying visualization supports this by showing that 44% of the founders of unicorn companies are non-US-born, with India (90) and Israel (52) being the top countries of origin, followed by China and Taiwan. This data suggests that the U.S. success in tech is significantly fueled by global talent.
author: Alec Stapp
content:
The US tech industry would be a shadow of itself without immigrants.

First 10 examples that come to mind:

1. Elon Musk (South Africa)

2. Andrej Karpathy (Czechoslovakia)

3. Sergey Brin (Russia)

4. Jensen Huang (Taiwan)

5. Satya Nadella (India)

6. Ilya Sutskever (Russia)

7. Sundar Pichai (India)

8. Lisa Su (Taiwan)

9. Fei-Fei Li (China)

10. Sanjay Mehrotra (India)

@AlecStapp wrote:
> Nearly half of the founders of billion-dollar tech startups are immigrants

Shaping up to be the biggest and most embarrassing geopolitical defeat in U.S. history. By a large margin.

title: A significant amount of the charm embodied in the 5000 years of urbanism before WWII exists in the urban form, not the m...
teaser: Marc Andreessen discusses the shift in economic power dynamics, noting that non-tech people are outperforming tech individuals in achieving fast revenue growth, a trend accelerated by the post-COVID era and advanced technology like AI.
summary: Marc Andreessen's composite post examines several modern societal and economic shifts. Key topics include the idea that the lasting charm of historical urbanism lies in its form, not its materials. More prominently, the post discusses the economic imbalance where 'non-tech normal people' are rapidly generating revenue more effectively than many tech-focused side projects. The post also points to the COVID-19 period as a defining moment marking a true step into the Future, driven by advancements in AI, drone warfare, and biotech. An anecdote is also shared about using AI (Claude) to simplify complex hardware procurement processes.
author: Marc Andreessen

title: Breaking: Young Princeton prof beats OpenAI at its own Erdos game, 3 days later.  here’s one sample, below, not even the...
teaser: Gary Marcus criticizes perceived intellectual dishonesty and misinformation directed at his research career, citing recent accusations about his active research output.
summary: Gary Marcus addresses what he views as a pattern of intellectually dishonest criticism regarding his career. He points to instances, such as a young Princeton professor reportedly surpassing OpenAI in an Erdos game, and counters claims questioning his research activity by mentioning recent publications in top journals like Science and the Proceedings of The Royal Society. He reiterates that he previously labeled such criticisms as 'propaganda,' particularly concerning the concept of scaling laws.
author: Gary Marcus
content:
Breaking: Young Princeton prof beats OpenAI at its own Erdos game, 3 days later.

here’s one sample, below, not even the only one I saw today; another claimed I don’t do research anymore when I had published articles in two top journals (Science and the Proceedings of The Royal Society) in the last 3 or 4 months.

title: AI does not need to be agentic to transform civilization completely; it just needs to be able to make matters of compete...
teaser: AI's transformative power comes from trivializing 'matters of competence,' not necessarily full agency. (via @diogenicvril)
summary: Montagnard, reposted by @pmarca, quotes @diogenicvril, who suggests that AI does not require full agency to transform civilization; rather, its power comes from trivializing matters of competence. The tweet also notes that those who fearmonger about AI exhibit low agency behavior, similar to ChatGPT.
author: Montagnard
